body_markdown:
AI-powered app development is becoming mainstream. According to the 2026 Stack Overflow survey,[65.9% of 17,464](https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2026/ai/data/ai-select) respondents reported using AI coding assistants or coding agents at work. For non-technical founders and businesses, platforms like[Floot](https://floot.com/) offer a way to build applications with databases, authentication, and hosting without manually configuring every backend service.


Choosing the right platform depends on more than generating an interface. This guide compares 13 AI app builders and backend platforms for 2027, examining their databases, AI development workflows, authentication, deployment capabilities, code portability, and pricing.


## **Key Takeaways**


- **Managed full-stack development:**[Floot's built-in services](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/whats-built-in) include PostgreSQL, authentication, file storage, email, and hosting, helping builders create applications with persistent data and user accounts.
- **Existing AI assistant workflows:** Through its[MCP connector](https://floot.com/integrations/mcp) , Floot supports development with Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations, subject to the connected client's permissions.
- **Separate building and infrastructure costs:** Floot uses daily building-action limits rather than a second AI build-credit bill for regular connector operations. Its[pricing plans](https://floot.com/en/pricing) also distinguish hosting allowances and optional AI credits.
- **Code and data ownership:** Floot users own their code, data, and intellectual property.[Database exports](https://floot.com/docs/faqs/code-data-and-exports) are available across plans, while downloading the complete project requires a paid subscription.
- **Web and mobile deployment:** Floot supports publishing web applications and provides[mobile app workflows](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/creating-mobile-apps-in-floot) for iOS and Android. App-store distribution requires the appropriate developer accounts and approval.


## **What to Look For in an AI App Builder with Backend APIs**


A reliable AI app builder should do more than produce frontend code. It should support the services required to run an application, including persistent storage, secure user access, APIs, hosting, and deployment. When evaluating platforms, consider these capabilities:


- **Database management:** Look for managed relational or NoSQL databases with appropriate querying, access controls, and backup options. PostgreSQL supports relationships and structured queries, while extensions such as pgvector support vector search. Floot's[managed database](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/whats-built-in) provides persistent data storage without separate database provisioning.
- **Authentication and security:** User accounts, session management, OAuth sign-in, and authorization controls matter for customer-facing applications. Evaluate encryption, secret management, and applicable compliance requirements. Floot documents its[security practices](https://floot.com/docs/platform/security-and-data) for app and user data.
- **Hosting and deployment:** Managed hosting, SSL, custom domains, and deployment workflows reduce infrastructure setup. Understand whether hosting uses fixed allowances or consumption-based billing. Floot provides guidance on[hosting costs](https://floot.com/docs/faqs/hosting) and usage.
- **Code ownership and portability:** Check whether code can be downloaded, databases exported, and projects self-hosted. Ownership does not necessarily mean every export option is available on a free plan. Floot explains its[export policies](https://floot.com/docs/faqs/code-data-and-exports) .
- **AI development workflows:** Some builders use an integrated AI agent, while others work through existing assistants. An[MCP connection](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) can let a supported assistant access project tools, although permissions and available actions vary by client.
- **Mobile deployment:** Determine whether the platform produces responsive web apps, installable web apps, or iOS and Android builds. App-store submission involves additional requirements, including developer accounts and platform review.


The following platforms take different approaches to these requirements.


## **1. Floot**


Floot is a full-stack app-building platform with an MCP connector that lets users create, edit, and publish applications through supported AI assistants, including Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations.


Floot provides managed infrastructure while the connected AI assistant handles development, with available building capabilities depending on the client's connector permissions.


### **How It Works**


Floot connects supported AI assistants to its application-building tools through the[Model Context Protocol](https://floot.com/blog/what-is-mcp-a-simple-guide-to-model-context-protocol-for-ai-apps) .


Builders can describe applications in natural language, request changes, inspect project files, test functionality, and publish applications through supported connector actions.


The connected assistant performs the development work, while Floot manages the project environment, infrastructure, and deployment.


### **Backend Capabilities**


- Managed PostgreSQL database for persistent application data
- Built-in authentication and user session management
- OAuth support for providers including Google and Microsoft
- CDN-backed file storage and managed hosting
- Transactional email, background jobs, and real-time features
- Payment integrations and custom domain support
- iOS and Android application-building workflows
- Database export and paid full-project ZIP downloads


Floot stores projects independently of individual AI conversations, allowing builders to continue development in later sessions. Its[built-in infrastructure](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/whats-built-in) is designed to reduce the need for manual service configuration.


### **Best For**


Floot is particularly suitable for:


- Non-technical founders building MVPs with saved data
- Small businesses creating internal tools and dashboards
- Operators developing custom CRMs and customer portals
- Teams already working with supported AI assistants
- Builders who need managed infrastructure and deployment
- Businesses requiring authentication, payments, and mobile workflows


### **Pricing**


Floot is free to start, with three main plans:


- **Free ($0/month):** 100 building actions per day, with access to core app-building and web publishing workflows.
- **Pro ($25/month):** 1,000 daily building actions, 5,000 monthly AI credits, and a $10 monthly hosting allowance.
- **Power ($100/month):** 5,000 daily building actions, 15,000 monthly AI credits, and a $25 monthly hosting allowance.


Building actions measure connector operations such as reading, editing, and testing. Failed actions do not count.


Regular connector-based development uses the connected assistant's own AI usage rather than a second Floot AI build-credit bill. Optional Floot AI features and AI functionality inside published apps can consume separate credits.


Hosting beyond included allowances is usage-billed. Mobile builds and app-store workflows have additional plan and developer-account requirements.


Review the current[Floot pricing here](https://floot.com/en/pricing) for more info.


## **2. Lovable**


Lovable is an AI app-building platform that creates applications using natural-language prompts. It supports React and TypeScript development, managed backend services, and code synchronization.


### **Primary Focus**


Lovable provides a prompt-driven development environment for generating and refining applications. It includes Lovable Cloud for managed backend functionality and supports connecting external Supabase projects.


### **Backend Capabilities**


- Managed database, authentication, and storage through Lovable Cloud
- Support for external Supabase integration
- PostgreSQL-backed data services
- GitHub synchronization for project code
- Application hosting and deployment
- Custom domains on eligible plans


### **App Building Considerations**


Lovable uses a credit-based AI development model. Its integrated cloud services and connected backend options may have separate usage considerations. Builders should review the selected backend configuration, database security, and export requirements before deployment.


For additional context, Floot provides a guide to[Lovable alternatives](https://floot.com/blog/best-lovable-alternatives-in-2026-apps-that-can-actually-ship) .


## **3. Bolt.new**


Bolt.new is a browser-based AI application builder that uses WebContainers technology to provide an interactive development environment.


### **Primary Focus**


Bolt enables users to generate, preview, and modify web applications through prompts. Its browser-based development environment supports rapid iteration without requiring a traditional local development setup.


### **Backend Capabilities**


- Bolt Cloud database services
- Authentication and managed hosting
- Node.js development through WebContainers
- Application preview and deployment
- Custom domains on eligible plans
- Database capacity and hosting allowances based on plan


### **App Building Considerations**


Bolt uses token-based AI usage limits. Backend configuration and deployment requirements depend on the application and selected cloud services. The development environment is useful for prompt-driven app creation, while production applications still require security and functionality testing.


Floot also provides a[Bolt comparison](https://floot.com/blog/floot-vs-bolt-which-ai-app-builder-is-better-in-2026) covering different app-building workflows.


## **4. Replit**


Replit combines a cloud-based coding environment with AI-assisted application development, managed databases, and deployment tools.


### **Primary Focus**


Replit provides a hosted development environment that supports both natural-language application generation and direct code editing. It combines its AI Agent with developer tools such as terminal access, package management, and version control.


### **Backend Capabilities**


- Managed PostgreSQL databases
- Development and production database environments
- Application hosting and deployment
- Terminal and package management tools
- Git-based development workflows
- Agent-assisted coding, debugging, and testing


### **App Building Considerations**


Replit supports users who want access to application code and development tools within a cloud workspace. AI-generated changes should be reviewed and tested before production deployment. Agent usage, deployment, and other resources can affect total costs.


For a workflow comparison, see[Floot vs Replit](https://floot.com/blog/floot-vs-replit-compare-ai-vibecoding-platforms-in-2026) .


## **5. Supabase**


Supabase is an open-source backend development platform built around PostgreSQL. It provides infrastructure for web and mobile applications rather than a complete prompt-to-app frontend builder.


### **Primary Focus**


Supabase serves developers and teams needing backend services for existing applications or custom frontend projects. Its PostgreSQL foundation supports relational data models, queries, and extensions for specialized functionality.


### **Backend Capabilities**


- Managed PostgreSQL databases
- Authentication and user management
- Row-level security policies
- File storage
- Edge Functions for server-side logic
- Real-time database subscriptions
- Vector search through pgvector
- Open-source and self-hosting options


### **App Building Considerations**


Supabase focuses on backend infrastructure. Teams generally need a separate frontend development workflow or application builder. Security policies, database queries, and production configuration remain important responsibilities for developers.


## **6. Base44**


Base44 is an AI app builder that creates frontend and backend functionality through natural-language instructions.


### **Primary Focus**


Base44 provides a prompt-to-deployment workflow with integrated application infrastructure. It is designed for users who want to create working applications without independently configuring databases, authentication, or hosting.


### **Backend Capabilities**


- Integrated application database
- Authentication and user management
- Managed hosting and deployment
- Application workflows and integrations
- Built-in storage
- Custom domains on eligible plans
- GitHub integration on Builder and higher plans


### **App Building Considerations**


Base44 uses separate message-credit and integration-credit allowances. Its development and export capabilities vary by subscription tier, so builders should review plan restrictions before committing to a long-term project.


Floot's[Base44 comparison](https://floot.com/blog/floot-vs-base44-which-ai-app-builder-is-better-in-2026) provides additional context about the two workflows.


## **7. Firebase**


Firebase is Google's application development platform, offering backend services, hosting, analytics, and integration with Google Cloud.


### **Primary Focus**


Firebase supports web and mobile development through managed backend services. It is particularly relevant for teams using Google Cloud infrastructure or requiring real-time application data and mobile development services.


### **Backend Capabilities**


- Cloud Firestore NoSQL database
- Firebase SQL Connect backed by PostgreSQL
- Firebase Authentication
- Cloud Functions and managed hosting
- Real-time data synchronization
- Firebase AI Logic for supported Gemini models
- Cloud Messaging for notifications
- Analytics and application monitoring


### **App Building Considerations**


Firebase supports both NoSQL and SQL-backed workflows. Firestore uses a document-oriented data model, while SQL Connect provides relational functionality through PostgreSQL. Teams should consider their data requirements, Google Cloud costs, and service configuration when choosing between these options.


## **8. v0**


v0 is Vercel's AI-assisted development platform for building React and Next.js applications.


### **Primary Focus**


v0 focuses on generating application interfaces and code through natural-language prompts. It supports visual editing, modern frontend development patterns, and deployment through Vercel.


### **Backend Capabilities**


- React and Next.js application generation
- Support for API routes and server-side functionality
- Server Actions and backend application logic
- Vercel deployment integration
- GitHub synchronization
- External database and storage integrations


### **App Building Considerations**


v0 can generate frontend and backend application code, but database infrastructure and other managed backend services may require additional integrations. The platform is relevant for teams working within the React, Next.js, and Vercel ecosystem.


## **9. Bubble**


Bubble is a visual no-code application development platform with built-in database management, workflows, and AI-assisted features.


### **Primary Focus**


Bubble enables users to build applications through visual editing and configurable workflows. It supports web applications and native mobile development, including projects that share backend data and logic.


### **Backend Capabilities**


- Visual database with custom data types
- Authentication and user management
- Workflow automation
- Application privacy rules
- API Connector for external services
- Managed hosting
- Native mobile application development
- Enterprise authentication options


### **App Building Considerations**


Bubble uses a proprietary visual development environment rather than generating a conventional exportable source-code project. Its workload-unit billing model also requires monitoring application resource usage.


For additional context, Floot offers a[Bubble comparison](https://floot.com/blog/floot-vs-bubble-which-no-code-platform-is-right-for-you-in-2026) .


## **10. Remy**


Remy is a specification-driven application builder developed by MindStudio. It uses a structured application specification to guide code generation and deployment.


### **Primary Focus**


Remy is designed for users who want to describe application requirements and maintain a structured specification throughout development. Its workflow uses AI agents to generate application code and coordinate development tasks.


### **Backend Capabilities**


- AI-assisted full-stack code generation
- Managed hosting and deployment
- Application databases
- Authentication services
- Specification-driven development
- AI model integrations
- Project code ownership and development workflows


### **App Building Considerations**


Remy separates application-building subscriptions from AI model inference costs. The specification-driven approach can help teams organize application requirements, but generated functionality still requires testing and review.


## **11. Convex**


Convex is a reactive backend platform designed for applications that require synchronized data and server-side functionality.


### **Primary Focus**


Convex focuses on reactive application data. Its query model can automatically update connected clients when relevant database information changes.


### **Backend Capabilities**


- Reactive database queries
- Real-time data synchronization
- TypeScript-based backend functions
- Built-in vector search
- File storage
- Scheduled functions
- Authentication integration
- Open-source and self-hosting options


### **App Building Considerations**


Convex uses its own database system rather than standard PostgreSQL. Its reactive model is useful for collaborative interfaces, live dashboards, and applications requiring frequently updated data. Teams should review its database model, query patterns, and portability requirements before adoption.


## **12. Hasura**


Hasura is a data API platform that exposes data through GraphQL and federated API infrastructure.


### **Primary Focus**


Hasura helps teams make existing application data accessible through APIs without manually implementing every endpoint. Its Data Delivery Network supports connecting multiple data sources into a unified API layer.


### **Backend Capabilities**


- GraphQL APIs over supported data sources
- PostgreSQL, MySQL, and SQL Server connectivity
- Federated data access through Hasura DDN
- Authorization and API access controls
- GraphQL subscriptions
- Data modeling and API management
- AI-oriented querying capabilities through PromptQL


### **App Building Considerations**


Hasura is primarily an API and data-access platform rather than a complete AI app builder. Teams generally need existing data sources and separate frontend development or application-building tools. Its pricing model also differs from fixed per-user subscriptions because paid DDN tiers can be based on active data models.


## **13. ChatGPT Sites**


ChatGPT Sites is a website and lightweight application-building capability available through eligible ChatGPT plans. It supports creating, editing, hosting, and sharing interactive experiences directly through ChatGPT.


### **Primary Focus**


ChatGPT Sites allows users to describe a website or application, review a preview, request changes, and publish it to a hosted URL. It supports interactive websites, dashboards, and other web applications without requiring a separate deployment service.


### **Backend Capabilities**


- Hosted website and application deployment
- Interactive pages and dashboards
- Site-level data storage
- Databases with documented storage limits
- Sharing and access controls
- Custom domains where available
- Integration with supported connected applications
- Source-code export through supported Codex workflows


### **App Building Considerations**


ChatGPT Sites supports stored data and can accommodate application sign-in features, but these capabilities should be evaluated against each application's authentication, data access, and backup requirements. Its database and publishing model differs from a separately managed PostgreSQL infrastructure service. Builders requiring specific relational database controls, application authentication workflows, or full-project portability should assess those requirements before deployment.


## **How Does Floot Help You Build and Publish a Full-Stack App?**


Floot helps non-technical founders, operators, and business owners turn application ideas into working software through supported AI assistants. Its[MCP integration](https://floot.com/integrations/mcp) lets a connected assistant work with application files, database structures, testing tools, and publishing actions while Floot provides the managed infrastructure.


With Floot, builders can:


- **Create full-stack applications** with persistent PostgreSQL data, user accounts, and[built-in services](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/whats-built-in) .
- **Develop through supported AI assistants** using natural-language instructions, subject to available connector permissions.
- **Publish applications** with managed hosting, SSL, and custom domain options.
- **Build mobile applications** using supported[iOS and Android workflows](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/creating-mobile-apps-in-floot) .
- **Retain ownership** of their code and data, with database exports and paid project downloads.


Floot is[free to start](https://floot.com/en/pricing) , so builders can explore an application before choosing a paid plan. Projects remain available for continued development, allowing users to refine functionality, fix issues, and publish updates through their connected assistant. Production applications should still be tested for security, reliability, and usability.


## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **What is an AI app builder with built-in backend APIs?**


An AI app builder with backend APIs helps create applications that can store data, authenticate users, and run server-side operations. Some platforms generate backend code, while others provide managed infrastructure. Floot includes a[managed PostgreSQL database](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/whats-built-in) , authentication, storage, and hosting, reducing the need to configure separate services.


### **Can existing Claude or ChatGPT subscriptions be used to build with Floot?**


Yes. Floot supports development through Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations using its MCP connector. The connected assistant handles development, while Floot manages application infrastructure. Available actions depend on the client's connector permissions. Floot's[connection guide](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) explains supported workflows and setup requirements.


### **How much does Floot cost, and are there separate AI charges?**


Floot is free to start. Its main plans are Free at $0/month, Pro at $25/month, and Power at $100/month. Regular connector-based building uses the connected AI assistant's usage allowance and Floot's building-action limits rather than a second Floot AI build-credit bill. Optional AI features and hosting beyond included allowances can result in additional costs. Review the current[pricing structure](https://floot.com/en/pricing) for plan details.


### **Who owns the code and data created with Floot?**


Floot users own their project code, application data, and intellectual property. Database export is available across plans. Downloading the complete project as a ZIP requires a paid subscription. The[code export guide](https://floot.com/docs/faqs/code-data-and-exports) explains how to access and download project data and source files.


### **Can Floot publish applications to the App Store and Google Play?**


Floot supports iOS and Android application-building workflows and provides options for preparing and submitting mobile builds. App-store distribution requires the appropriate Apple Developer and Google Play developer accounts, along with compliance with each store's publishing requirements. Submission does not guarantee approval. Floot's[mobile app guide](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/creating-mobile-apps-in-floot) explains the build and distribution process.
